event.felix_heart2.0.text: Mornin'. You're shaking. Here. Take the rod, both hands. Something to hold onto helps.
event.felix_heart2.0.why: frightened: he sees a shaken person and gives them a practical job

event.felix_heart2.0.text: Mornin'. You look like you slept on the rocks. Take the rod. Both hands. It steadies a person.

event.felix_heart2.1.text: Feel that? Don't reel yet. It's running for the shore, not the sea. They've done that lately. Let it run.
event.felix_heart2.1.why: hint: fish heading the wrong way, noticed not explained

event.felix_heart5.0.text: Every fisher has a lucky charm. Mine's sat through forty years of dawns. A few quiet ones, lately.
event.felix_heart5.0.why: uneasy: his fear (a quiet dawn) touched lightly

event.felix_heart5.1.text: It was mine. It's yours now. You look like you need it more. Keep it in a pocket. Near.
event.felix_heart5.1.why: frightened: the gift becomes comfort for someone who looks unwell

event.felix_heart5.2.text: Fair winds. ...Someday I'll show you the boat. She leaks, but politely. Won't leave the dock on new moons, though.
event.felix_heart5.2.why: hint: the boat that won't leave on the new moon; he treats it as a boat's mood

event.past_the_point.0.text: There you both are. I promised you the boat. She's ready. Fog's thick past the point, so we keep the shore in sight.
event.past_the_point.0.why: uneasy: the morning fog that lingers, met with seamanship

event.past_the_point.4.text: Dawn's better with two. With three, it's an expedition. ...From out there, the wood looked closer. Light plays tricks. I'll want a bigger boat.
event.past_the_point.4.why: hint: the woods seem closer, shrugged off as light

event.story_whistler_felix.intro.text: Oh. You heard that. ...Good. I thought the lane was whistling back. Don't tell the fish.
event.story_whistler_felix.intro.why: uneasy: an echo he cannot place; relief that it was the player

dlg.story.whistler.felix.0.text: I only whistle when I'm happy. Or when evenings go too quiet. Lately, both. ...The happy part I could explain.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.0.why: hint: evenings have gone quiet; the romantic tease kept

dlg.story.whistler.felix.1.text: ...Well? Say something. Please. The quiet's worse tonight.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.1.why: frightened: the joke becomes a real request

dlg.story.whistler.felix.r2.text: You listened. The whole tune. Nobody's done that but the pond. The pond's gone quiet lately. ...I may whistle again.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.r2.why: uneasy: the pond, his oldest listener, has stopped answering

event.story_whistler_felix.after.text: Same hour tomorrow, same lane. Before dark, mind. I'll walk you to the corner. You can pretend you were passing.
event.story_whistler_felix.after.why: frightened: he follows the village's home-before-dark habit without explaining it

event.story_pumpkin_felix.intro.text: Ah. Caught. I only borrowed it. For scale, beside my biggest carp. ...Tilda's patch grows odd shapes lately. I wanted a look.
event.story_pumpkin_felix.intro.why: hint: odd crop shapes, noticed by the least botanical man in town

dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.0.text: Behind the store, Felix stands beside a very large pumpkin, wearing a very guilty face. The pumpkin leans, a little, toward the wood.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.0.why: uneasy: narration gives a wrong-leaning detail and lets it pass

event.story_pumpkin_felix.after.text: Back it goes. ...You've gone quiet, [player]. Come by the stall after. I'll make tea. Fish-free, even.
event.story_pumpkin_felix.after.why: frightened: the closing joke gives way to care

event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.text: My wish is small this year. A whole night's sleep. For all of us. ...Wishes shrink, sometimes.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.why: frightened: no one sleeps through the night; the tall tale turned inside out

event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.text: My wish is this big. Last winter it was this big. ...Lanterns lean toward the wood this year. Wind, likely.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.2.why: hint: the lanterns drift the wrong way, explained away

event.felix_heart8.intro.text: The pond, and a line that's tugging. I've had a feeling all week. Not all of it good. Hold the net. Don't breathe.
event.felix_heart8.intro.why: uneasy: his week-long feeling has a shadow in it

dlg.felix.big.0.text: Something very large tugs on Felix's line. It might be a fish. It might be the bottom. The bottom of the pond.
dlg.felix.big.0.why: frightened: the shipped joke with one repeated fragment of distortion

dlg.felix.big.1.text: It's this big. No, this big. ...It's pulling toward the trees. Partner, what do we do?
dlg.felix.big.1.why: hint: the fish faces the wood

dlg.felix.big.r1.text: Let it go? ...Right. A good fish deserves a long life. Off it goes, toward the wood bank. We keep the story.
dlg.felix.big.r1.why: uneasy: the release keeps its meaning; the direction is odd

event.felix_heart8.after.text: {if choice:big.net}Netted. It was this big. By Friday it'll be this big. Odd, though. It kept looking at the trees.{else}{if choice:big.release}Gone home. Straight for the wood bank. Same dawn next year, we said. We've an understanding.{else}Eleven inches. Honest inches. Faced the trees the whole time. I'm devastated. And proud.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_heart8.after.why: hint in every branch: the fish faces the wood; each choice's payoff kept

event.felix_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.felix.wish}Two well-wishers before noon. Tilda, then you. You looked pale saying it. Sit a while.{else}{if choice:bday.felix.story}The story's longer now. I added you at the end, holding the net. Safe and dry. That's the ending.{else}Tomorrow, then, off the good rock. Best present I've had. Come early. Dawns are easier with company.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_birthday.after.why: frightened: each branch ends on plain care for the player

event.felix_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.felix.shell}The shell sits on my shelf, by the best hook. It hums at night, lately. Still says your name, though.{else}{if choice:courtship.felix.fish}One very small fish, all morning. The fog never lifted. We threw it back. I've already made it bigger.{else}The sun came late through the fog. We waited anyway. Longest conversation I've ever had.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_partners.after.why: uneasy: the hum and the fog that stays, with the warmth intact

event.felix_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. Tilda says no fishing today. She brought a pie. You look tired. Sit. I brought a story about a fish.
event.felix_birthday.intro.why: uneasy: he notices the player's tiredness on his own day

dlg.felix.birthday.r1.text: Sit, then. It was dawn, it was this big, and it was smirking at me. Facing the wood, too. Odd fish.

dlg.felix.birthday.r2.text: Dawn tomorrow. Bring a line. I'll bring the good rock. And a blanket. You look like you need a long sit.

event.felix_courtship.intro.text: Well. Right. I've held a line through a gale. This is harder. You look worn, so I'll be quick. Would you court me? Slowly.
event.felix_courtship.intro.why: uneasy: he sees the player is worn and keeps it short

event.felix_courtship2.intro.text: Second cast, then. You asked for time, and I gave it. Long nights lately, for everyone. Would you court me? Still slowly.
event.felix_courtship2.intro.why: uneasy: the village is sleeping badly; he offers steadiness

dlg.felix.partners.0.text: Tide's out. Fog's in. Morning's still ours. What'll it be?

dlg.felix.partners.r0.text: Hear it? That's the sea. ...Or something low under it. I'd rather it said your name. Let's say it does.
dlg.felix.partners.r0.why: frightened: the hum under the shell; he chooses the kind reading

dlg.felix.partners.r0.text: Hear it? That's the sea. It hums low, lately. Steady, though. I think it's saying your name.
dlg.felix.partners.r0.why: uneasy: the low hum, held at arm's length

event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l2.text: It's a bigger carp. It grew. Overnight, facing the wood. Out of pride, I expect.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_1.l2.why: hint: animals face the wood, folded into the joke

event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l3.text: Same winter. A long one. You brought me soup. Both times. And left the lamp on.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_2.l3.why: hint: points the player at Tilda's lamp without knowing why it matters

event.overheard_tilda_felix_3.l3.text: I chalked it life-size. Then I added a hand. The pond's been quiet lately. Don't tell it.

event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l1.text: Tilda. I brought a pie. Early, since you're closing early. Again. New moon, is it?
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l1.why: hint on ritual day only: the store closing early on the new moon, asked innocently

event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l1.text: Elara. A fish doesn't want a cozy net. It wants to be free. Mine want the shallows lately.

event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l1.text: Three feet, nose to tail. Last spring it was two. Fewer of them this spring, though.
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l1.why: uneasy: fewer fish, the big one still growing

event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l1.text: Dawn's too quiet lately. No gulls. So count your stitches out loud.
event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l1.why: uneasy: birds quieter; Elara's counting becomes welcome noise

adds.text: Funny. No gulls this morning. They'd usually be on that tuna before you.
adds.why: hint: birds quieter, as a fisher would notice

adds.text: Your great-uncle sat on that rock some dawns. Never fished. Just watched the tree line. Odd man. Kind.
adds.why: clue edge: an unaware witness of Edmund watching the wood; points at Dorian's 'counting the trees' without explaining

adds.text: Sit in the middle, [player]. You're pale. Water's flat today. Nothing out here but us.
adds.why: frightened: reassurance that reads slightly too hopeful

threads.felix_heart2: Why are the fish running for the shore and the gulls gone?
threads.felix_heart5: Why won't Felix's boat leave the dock on new moons, and what was Edmund watching in the tree line?
threads.past_the_point: Why did the wood look closer from the water?
threads.story_whistler_felix: What answered Felix's whistle in the lane, and why must everyone be home before dark?
threads.story_pumpkin_felix: Why do Tilda's crops grow odd and lean toward the wood?
threads.festival_winter_lanterns: Why do the lanterns drift toward the wood, and why is nobody sleeping?
threads.felix_heart8: What in the pond pulls toward the trees?
threads.felix_birthday: Why do the fish all face the wood?
threads.felix_courtship: What is making the player, and the village, so tired?
threads.felix_courtship2: Why is everyone in Wetherell sleeping badly?

threads.overheard_tilda_felix_2: Who is Tilda's lamp really for?
threads.overheard_tilda_felix_3: Why has the pond gone quiet?

notes: felix_heart5 add invents a small Edmund detail (sat on Felix's rock at dawn watching the tree line). It echoes 'counting the trees' without duplicating it; strike it if LORE.md says Edmund never came to the beach.

Round 3b: branched .after variants added for felix_heart8, felix_birthday and felix_partners (all branches kept). felix_courtship.after and felix_courtship2.after left plain on purpose: the answer to a proposal should stay clean.
overheard_tilda_felix_4.l1 variant uses day==4 so it plays only on the new-moon day (store closes early). Felix only asks; he never explains.
Choice labels left alone on purpose, so the meaning of every choice stays the same.
